extracted.intended_audience: writers and critics of short fiction, anthology editors, literary scholars, and librarians
extracted.subtask_description: Critical-selection and review criteria for short stories and short-story collections (what makes an individual story or an anthology 'best' or noteworthy). Includes procedural selection notes (marking, exclusion of reprints) and many stylistic, formal, and editorial quality criteria illustrated with examples from contemporary authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and marking conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories of special excellence are indicated by an asterisk; index figures prefixed to the name of the author indicate previous inclusion in prior Rolls of Honor (1914–1919); the list excludes reprints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural rules for assembling the Roll of Honor and marking exceptional items. Use the asterisk to flag special excellence; track repeat inclusions by year-index figures; exclude reprinted material when compiling a year's distinctive list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of reprints
rubrics_metrics.description: The list excludes reprints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging the year's short stories, credit only new publications rather than reprints; this preserves focus on new work and prevents double-counting prior merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy of means / economy of detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories praised for being 'told with the utmost economy of means' or showing 'economy of detail' are judged technically successful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concise, economical presentation—avoid unnecessary elaboration. Examples: stories that achieve effect with tightly controlled detail (e.g., 'A Simple Act of Piety'; 'The Maternal Feminine' praised for economy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Successful use of dialogue-only form
rubrics_metrics.description: A short story written entirely in dialogue can be 'technically interesting' and 'thoroughly successful' when it sustains narrative, character, and dramatic shape.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using an all-dialogue form, ensure clarity of speakers, progression of action, and sufficient dramatic contrast so the story remains coherent (example praised: 'The Ditch' as a dialogue story).

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth of conception and breadth of execution
rubrics_metrics.description: Works with 'depth of conception and breadth of execution' are valued — broad, profound ideas rendered with ample scope and craft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess both the idea's substantive richness and the author's ability to realize it across structure, character, and language (example: Irvin S. Cobb's work compared favorably for these qualities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity and convincing voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that feel grounded in first-hand experience or truthful dialect ('based on a background of first-hand experience', 'told by the wharf-rat in dialect with a casual reportorial air') are commended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voice should be convincing and appropriate to setting and character; dialect and colloquialism must ring true rather than caricature. Authentic detail supports credibility (example: Hiker Joy's dialect narrator).

rubrics_metrics.name: Durability / lasting literary value
rubrics_metrics.description: Some stories are judged 'destined to last' and compared to canonical models; lasting value is a criterion distinct from immediate popularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether a story's themes, craft, and insight will endure beyond topicality—does it belong alongside long-standing masters (examples: stories said to rival Hawthorne and Poe)?

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal innovation versus adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Pieces that 'answer to no usual concepts of literary form' may necessitate creation of a new form; judges note when a book is not really 'short stories' but another literary mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether formal departures succeed: do they create a coherent new mode or simply fail to meet short-story expectations? Innovation is praise only when effective (example: Dreiser's 'Twelve Men' creating a different form).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restraint and compositional control
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical merit shown by quietly set details 'without undue emphasis' and 'selective presentation of aspects in character'; finished composition and controlled presentation are praised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overstatement and melodrama; allow craftful restraint to reveal rather than shout. Look for careful arrangement of detail and measured emphasis (example: H. G. Dwight's quiet compositional control).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial curation and compression
rubrics_metrics.description: Anthologies are judged on editorial decisions: omission of weak items, compression of inferior or superfluous material, and the editor's hand in shaping a representative collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good anthologies should omit irrelevant or weak pieces and tighten scope; editors should aim for coherence and representative quality rather than exhaustive inclusion (criticisms: collections 'would have gained measurably by compression'; 'very badly edited collection').

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of material to author's gifts
rubrics_metrics.description: An author's 'fertility of imagination' can be wasted on 'unworthy material'; conversely, choice of material that fits the writer's strengths is praised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether subject matter suits the author's sensibility and technique—imaginative power must be applied to material worthy of it, or the work will feel squandered (example: Robbins' imagination vs. unworthy material).

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre technique and suspense construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Genre stories (mystery, ghost, psychic) are judged on technical mastery of their conventions—'inevitable relentlessness of plot', 'quality of suspense', etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For genre fiction, evaluate how effectively conventions are used (plot inevitability, suspense pacing, revelation mechanics). Mastery of genre technique can place a work among the best (example: Melville Davisson Post's mystery technique compared to Poe).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive personal style and originality
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'personal style built up out of nervous rhythms and an instinctive reticence' or other distinctive registers is a mark of high achievement and significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for an individualized voice and formal fingerprints—original rhythm, diction, or perspective that distinguish the writer from influences (example: Willa Cather's personal style).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtle and penetrating characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: Subtlety of portraiture and 'penetrating analysis of character' are prized; fine characterization can lift sketches into high art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge depth and nuance in depiction of persons—the ability to render character by implication, gesture, and select detail (examples: Arthur Johnson's subtle portraiture; Alvin Johnson's penetrating analysis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of substance with environment/setting
rubrics_metrics.description: An author's 'ability to subdue his substance to the environment in which it is set' is praised—successful merging of character/material with setting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether setting and environment enhance and shape the material rather than merely decorating it; harmony between subject and milieu is a mark of craft (example: Arthur Johnson's work).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional control and tonal balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticisms include being 'emotionally overtaut', 'too repressed', or 'tone is too neutral to be altogether convincing'; emotional balance is crucial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether emotional tone matches the story's aims—neither overwrought nor anaemic. Effective restraint and appropriate intensity are signs of maturity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective organizing principle and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that take 'some tiny and apparently insignificant happening which altered the whole course of a life' or that use a deliberate method of presentation are commended for structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for a clear organizing idea or structural device that gives the story coherence and resonance; a subtle pivot or unifying conceit that justifies the story's shape (example: O'Higgins' studies 'From the Life').

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of overt propagandist statement; prefer suggestion
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'definite propagandist aim is usually fatal to fiction,' whereas 'deft suggestion rather than underscored statement' can succeed even with propagandist material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When fiction has an agenda, prefer implicit dramatization and suggestion; overt didacticism weakens artistic effect (example: Ellen N. La Motte succeeds by suggestion rather than underscoring her aim).

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative selection and breadth for anthologies
rubrics_metrics.description: An anthology should represent a 'fair cross-section' of the year's short stories if that is its aim; selections may legitimately include 'good, bad, and indifferent' to show range.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether the anthology's purpose is representative surveying or selective canonizing; a representative anthology should include diversity of quality and form, while a 'best of' list should be more discriminating (example: O. Henry Memorial volume described as a fair cross-section).

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical/historical interest versus artistic merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Some pieces are valuable 'either as early studies for later stories, or for their biographical value' even when not artistically top-tier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize different kinds of value—historical or biographical importance can justify inclusion even when artistic achievement is modest (example: recovered early O. Henry pieces).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for educational use versus permanent value
rubrics_metrics.description: Volumes compiled for schools ('supplementary reading for secondary schools') may have pedagogic aims and include pieces not of the highest permanent literary value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate selections intended for instruction (clarity, accessibility, illustrative qualities) from those chosen for lasting literary significance; evaluate according to intended function (example: 'Short Stories of the New America').
